entities.summary: Alinah Kelo Segobye is a renowned social development activist and archaeologist who has dedicated her career to understanding the intersection of social development and HIV/AIDS in Africa. Born into a family of intellectuals, Segobye pursued her passion for social justice and cultural preservation at the University of Namibia, where she earned a degree in archaeology. Her groundbreaking research on the cultural legacy of colonialism in Namibia has been widely cited and has influenced policy decisions at the national and international levels. As Dean of Human Sciences at the Namibia University of Science and Technology, Segobye has fostered a new generation of scholars and activists committed to social development and cultural preservation. Through her work, Segobye has received numerous awards and accolades, including the prestigious Fellowship of the African Academy of Sciences, which recognizes her tireless efforts to promote social development and cultural preservation in Africa. Segobye's legacy extends beyond her own work, as she has inspired a new wave of social development activists and archaeologists who are committed to preserving the cultural heritage of Africa and promoting social justice and equality.
